lines: My daughter is subscribed to a hundred and forty-eight YouTube channels. I had seen about ten of them. Her brother follows nineteen.
No parent can check a hundred and forty-eight channels, so nobody does. Parental controls decide what a child may see, and then do nothing.
HeyGilli is the agent that does that job for you.
A parent answers a few questions about what is fine in their house, and picks what the child likes.
That is all the setup there is.
Then the Curator agent reads each new upload from the family's channels, against those answers.
Clear cases it decides alone, and it shows its reasons as tags a parent can skim.
Anything it kept back says why.
Borderline videos wait for the parent, with the reason in two sentences.
That is the whole relationship. The agent does the work. The parent answers only the questions that are really theirs.
Found a video yourself? Paste the link, and Gilli reads it against your answers before your child ever sees it.
The child's shelf looks like YouTube Kids, with only what the parent allowed.
They can search, by typing or by voice, but only among those videos. Search never reaches YouTube.
At a natural break the video pauses, and Gilli asks one question about what just happened, out loud.
The Planner agent wrote it for this video and this child's age.
The child answers by talking or by tapping, and the Buddy agent replies, then the video carries on.
A younger child gets big pictures, and questions that need no reading: one word, a tap, or a yes or no.
A right answer gets a cheer. A wrong one gets curiosity. Nobody is ever told they are wrong.
The parent sets the day's minutes, where the breaks fall, and when the day ends.
None of that is the model's to decide. The limits are the parent's, and the code is what enforces them.
Between videos there are two short games. The Playmate agent picks how hard the next round is. Where Gilli hides is picked in code.
Each night the Digest agent reads the day and writes a short note for the parent:
what was said, what was only heard, and one question to ask at dinner.
Every agent's model is one line of configuration.
Today that is Amazon Nova Pro on Amazon Bedrock, the one our eval picked. Change the line, and the same agents run on another model.
Eight Strands agents sit behind one gateway: Curator, Planner, Buddy, Digest, Reviewer, Coach, Explainer and Playmate.
The agents decide. The code fetches and enforces, because the guarantees a parent trusts belong in code, not in a prompt.
Ads still play, and creators still get paid.
Nothing a child says is stored. Only a score and a short paraphrase.
HeyGilli. Try it at heygilli dot com. The code and a three-part write-up are in the description.
